title: What parts of your game do you refuse to use AI for, even if you could?
author: SysPsych
selftext:
Whether because AI solutions aren't there yet, or you just plain prefer to do it yourself.

For me, it's anything related to writing. The most I'll do is ask for the AI to read what I've written and point out flaws or strengths, and even then, just because I don't want to bother other actual humans with my stuff. Otherwise, I want 100% control.

Another thing is certain kinds of animations. Anything exaggerated or cartoony, I think, really needs human intervention to nail timing or have personality. So this is where I'm pulling out Moho or Blender more often than not.

Just curious what parts other people want control over, even if they're otherwise comfortable with AI use.

replies.author: throwaway098242
replies.body:
Be careful with that, it's not. They're called Large Language Models for a reason. Large Language Models, not Large Number Models.

Remember when they couldn't even do multiplication when they came out? Yeah, they still can't. The trick is that they just call into external tools (calculators, scripts, ...) to achieve these tasks. This is fine if you just need the result to do some stuff with it, e.g. it's perfect if you ask the LLM to "Compare available health insurances and make me a table with the top 10 cheapest options". That's basically just a fuzzy for-loop that transfers data from representation A to representation B, which LLMs are very good at because this happens in language all the time.

Asking it to do balancing is a wildly different task to what it was trained on. The LLM architecture is built for doing sequence-to-sequence translation, e.g. give it a text and it outputs the rest of it, not for manipulating numbers.

Is there anything you could recommend me? Some awesome items to test? Some good online sfx libraries worth looking into? Maybe something else I should look into?.. thanks..

replies.author: Friend135
replies.body: I use a variety of sources for my design material.  I record my own props (my dad has a wood working studio that has lots of interesting sounding tools in it!), I download free sound packs from the internet (most notably the GDC free sound FX library), and peruse various websites for good deals on sound effect packs (A Sound Effect is a favorite of mine).  Also, I have various plugins that have some unique sounds that I mix together with the aforementioned sources to create unique material for SFX.

comments.author: oadephon

I had a couple of writing brainstorming sessions with Claude and realized that if I don't come up with the idea, it just doesn't appeal to me. It has to come out of my brain or I won't even want to stick it into the game.

comments.author: Elegant_Bonbon
comments.body: AI is still really bad at story writing. Theme and plotting especially. AI also dislikes leaving conflict unsolved and 'toxic' situations so it tries to solve conflicts in the same scene, and tends to default to Saturday Morning Cartoon level writing, you know simple conflicts, a Very Special Lesson, and characters articulating the Lesson out loud. AI also tends to flatten characters into stereotypes. All of this is so annoying I tested AI writing and noped back to writing by myself lol

comments.author: WindFlow_H
comments.body:
Personally, I don't want to use AI-generated stuff directly in any part of the art process or game design. I think one of the things that makes indie games special is the personality of the people behind them. AI-generated content just doesn't really have that personal touch from my perspective.

I'm not against using AI as a tool, though. I think it's fine when it's just helping with the workflow, rather than doing the actual creative work. Something like generating in-between frames based on keyframes I've drawn myself, for example, would be relatively fine with me.

replies.author: SysPsych
replies.body:
I'm in this boat. Accent on the 'directly'. Even an AI image that is pretty good, I'm going to take into post and chop it up, work on it.

That's the big trap I see with AI. It can very quickly get you to 75-85% of the job being done. Calling it 'good enough' there instead of picking up from where it left off and finishing it right is just not for me.

comments.author: Razrie
comments.body:
Personally I dont use it for story, decisions or concepts.  Im fine using it for coding, art, and design.  I wish it was more consistent, that would be the only reason to want an artist involved.  But as someone that is more interested in game design from mechanics and story.  I can visualize the characters in my head, and honestly telling someone draw me exactly this, is no different then telling ai to do it.

Because I dont care about that artists style or personality, I also can not name a single artist from any of the thousands of games I've played.  I have never looked at the credits, I dont care who you are. Exceptions being probably only toriyama.  I want the character to meet my design choices.  Well draw it yourself!  People will say... and honestly im sorry but thats stupid.  Ugly shit content is not good for me, or the audience.  And im not going to spend years practicing just to make art for an indie game im solo devving.  And coding... well lets be honest here this is menial grunt work.  If you enjoy it thats fine, people enjoy working on engines, or gardening, or whatever.  You can add fluffy "oh the artistry, the soul, the spirit, whatever" but thats just pretentious and you are using fluff words to invoke a feeling in someone when all you are doing is sitting around pushing buttons on a keyboard.

I did use it to build dialogue for my game to start.  Because I needed a lot of conversations that were just daily relationship point grinders.  But I wrote their and the games main storylines.

comments.author: satupidfukignidot
comments.body:
My models & animations for playable characters.

Tech isn't remotely there. Fixing a Tripo or Meshy model is the same size job, if not bigger. There is no equivalent to inpainting for 3d. All of this means I'd be effectively asking to make the task harder, for worse results, and likely a comparable cost.

Also, core gameplay element design is up there. If you can't come up with a solid loop for a game, what makes you think you can come up with decent GaaS content?
